keywords.def: time that parents arrange for their young children to play together
small group of people who like to spend a lot of time together and may seem unfriendly towards other people
(informal) short for glamorous: visually attractive and exciting
belong and feel accepted by the other people in a group
(informal) depend on chance rather than effort or skill
quickly feel a friendly connection with someone, especially the first time you meet them

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好。这里是 BBC 英语教学的“6分钟英语”。

sentences.en: I’m Neil. And I’m Beth. Do you remember your first day at school, Neil?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是贝丝。尼尔，你还记得你上学的第一天吗？

sentences.en: Um, yes I do. I changed schools quite a lot when I was a kid, so I had lots of first days and they were never easy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，记得。我小时候转过很多次学，所以经历过很多个第一天，而且它们从来都不轻松。

sentences.en: How about you, Beth? Well, my mum always tells this story about how I was crying a lot on my first day.
sentences.zh: 你呢，贝丝？嗯，我妈妈总是讲这样一个故事：我第一天去学校的时候哭得很厉害。

sentences.en: But apparently as soon as she left, I was quite happy.
sentences.zh: 但显然她一离开，我就挺高兴的。

sentences.en: So my mum spent the day being a bit sad and I was completely fine.
sentences.zh: 所以我妈花了一整天时间闷闷不乐，而我则完全没事。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, starting school and making new friends is difficult for many children.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对许多孩子来说，开始上学和结交新朋友确实很难。

sentences.en: But it’s not just the kids who find it challenging.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是孩子们觉得这很有挑战性。

sentences.en: For mums and dads who drop their kids off at the school gates in the morning and pick them up again at the end of the school day, making friends with other mums can be just as hard.
sentences.zh: 对于那些早上把孩子送到校门口、放学时又把他们接回家的爸爸妈妈们来说，和其他妈妈交朋友同样不容易。

sentences.en: Here, BBC presenter, Nuala McGovern, discusses this problem using the term, ‘mum friends’.
sentences.zh: 在这里，BBC 主持人努拉·麦戈文（Nuala McGovern）用“妈妈朋友”（‘mum friends’）这个词探讨了这个问题。

sentences.en: So if you are a mum dropping off or picking up the kids this week, how do you feel about hanging out with other ‘mum friends’?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这周你是送孩子上学或接孩子放学的妈妈，你对和其它“妈妈朋友”一起闲逛有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I find that term kind of interesting as well, mum friends – they’re never called ‘friends’, they’re called ‘mum friends’.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得这个词挺有意思的，“妈妈朋友”——她们从来不叫“朋友”，而是叫“妈妈朋友”。

sentences.en: Do you struggle to make those relationships, or do you thrive on them, or are you perfectly happy without them?
sentences.zh: 你在维系这些关系时感到挣扎吗？还是乐在其中？又或者没有它们你也过得挺开心？

sentences.en: ‘Mum friends’ are usually the mums of other children in your child’s class at school.
sentences.zh: “妈妈朋友”通常指你孩子在学校同班同学的其他妈妈。

sentences.en: They might go for coffee together, help out with babysitting or chat about being a mother.
sentences.zh: 她们可能会一起去喝咖啡、帮忙照看孩子或是聊聊当母亲的心得。

sentences.en: But is making new ‘mum friends’ really the positive experience it’s often described as, or an additional stress for already overworked mothers?
sentences.zh: 但是，结交新的“妈妈朋友”真的像人们常说的那样是一段积极的经历，还是给本来就工作过度的母亲们增添了额外的压力？

sentences.en: That’s what we’ll be discussing in this programme, along with some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在本期节目中要讨论的内容，此外还有一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And if the idea of ‘mum friends’ is new to you, why not take a minute to read through the list of vocabulary before you listen?
sentences.zh: 如果你对“妈妈朋友”这个概念感到陌生，为什么不在收听之前花一分钟通读一下词汇列表呢？

sentences.en: It’s easy to find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 这很容易在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

sentences.en: Now I have a question for you, Beth. Another term often associated with ‘mum friends’ is play date – a time that parents arrange for their children to play together.
sentences.zh: 现在我有一个问题要问你，贝丝。另一个常与“妈妈朋友”联系在一起的词是“play date”（玩伴约会）——这是父母为孩子们安排的一起玩耍的时间。

sentences.en: But according to the Oxford English Dictionary, where does the term come from?
sentences.zh: 但根据《牛津英语词典》，这个词源自哪里？

sentences.en: Is the origin in: a) Australia? b) New Zealand? or, c) the United States of America?
sentences.zh: 它的起源是：a) 澳大利亚？b) 新西兰？还是 c) 美利坚合众国？

sentences.en: Um, I'm gonna guess the USA, C. OK. Feeling confident?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我猜是美国，C。好的。很有信心吗？

sentences.en: Yes! Well, we'll see at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 对！好吧，我们在节目结束时拭目以待。

sentences.en: For some mums, dropping their kids off at school reminds them of when they themselves were little and under pressure to make friends.
sentences.zh: 对某些妈妈来说，把孩子送到学校会勾起她们自己小时候面对交友压力的回忆。

sentences.en: Listen as mum, Jayne Cherrington-Cook, describes these feelings to BBC Radio 4 programme, Woman’s Hour: The school gates take you back to being back at school.
sentences.zh: 听听妈妈杰恩·切林顿-库克（Jayne Cherrington-Cook）在 BBC 第四台节目《女性时间》（Woman’s Hour）中对这种感受的描述：校门口会把你带回上学的时候。

sentences.en: It's like you said, a high school clique.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，就像一个高中死党小圈子。

sentences.en: You’ve got the sporty mums over there, you’ve got the glam mums over there, you've got, you know… And if you don't fit into one of those it's really, really difficult to navigate, and yet you're all there just because your children were born in the same year.
sentences.zh: 那边是运动型的妈妈，那边是迷人的妈妈，还有，你知道的……如果你不属于其中任何一类，那就真的、真的很难融入，然而你们聚在一起仅仅是因为你们的孩子生在同一年。

sentences.en: It's a really weird thing! Jayne says that mums often form cliques, small groups of people who like spending time together and seem unfriendly towards others.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一件很诡异的事！杰恩说妈妈们经常形成小圈子（cliques），也就是一群喜欢花时间待在一起、对其他人显得很不友好的人。

sentences.en: For example, at Jayne’s daughter’s school there’s a clique of sporty mums, and a clique of glam mums who put on make-up and dress up.
sentences.zh: 例如，在杰恩女儿的学校里，有一个运动型妈妈的小圈子，还有一个精心化化妆、打扮得漂漂亮亮的迷人妈妈的小圈子。

sentences.en: Jayne uses the adjective glam as a shortened form of the word, glamour, meaning attractive and exciting.
sentences.zh: 杰恩用形容词 glam 作为 glamour（迷人、激动人心）的缩写，意思是迷人和吸引人。

sentences.en: Problems start when someone doesn’t fit into one of the cliques.
sentences.zh: 当有人无法融入这些小圈子时，问题就出现了。

sentences.en: If you fit into a group of people, you feel you belong and are accepted, probably because you are similar to them.
sentences.zh: 如果你能融入一个群体，你会觉得自己属于并被接纳，这可能是因为你和他们很相似。

sentences.en: So some mums feel rejected from cliques and worry about their children being left out of play dates.
sentences.zh: 所以有些妈妈会因为被小圈子排斥而感到难过，并担心自己的孩子在玩伴约会被冷落。

sentences.en: But other mums don’t mind – if people want to be friends that’s fine, and if they don’t, that’s fine too!
sentences.zh: 但其他妈妈并不介意——如果别人想交朋友，那很好；如果不想，也没关系！

sentences.en: Being a mum is hard enough without adding more stress.
sentences.zh: 当妈妈已经够难的了，没必要再给自己增添压力。

sentences.en: Jayne definitely belongs to this group, as she explains to BBC Radio 4’s, Woman’s Hour: I think I'd had some really bad experiences at baby groups where you're trying to make your child do yoga or paint when they're four months old, and trying to bond with these other women and I just thought, ‘This is ridiculous!’ And I pretty much straight away realised it was gonna be just down to luck if I met somebody that I clicked with.
sentences.zh: 杰恩显然属于后一种，正如她向 BBC 第四台《女性时间》节目所解释的那样：我想我之前在育儿小组里有过一些非常糟糕的经历，当孩子四个月大的时候，你得让他们学瑜伽或画画，还要努力和这些女人搞好关系，我当时就想：“这太荒谬了！”我几乎立刻就意识到，能不能遇到一个合得来的人全凭运气。

sentences.en: Jayne says it’s down to luck if she makes mum friends.
sentences.zh: 杰恩说能不能交到妈妈朋友全凭运气。

sentences.en: If you say something is down to luck, you mean it depends on chance rather than any skill or effort you make.
sentences.zh: 如果你说某事是“down to luck”（全凭运气），意思是它取决于机缘巧合，而不是你的任何技巧或努力。

sentences.en: But there’s always the possibility you’ll meet someone and click with them, become friends as soon as you start talking.
sentences.zh: 但总有一种可能性，你会遇到某人并和对方“click”（一拍即合），一聊起来就成了朋友。

sentences.en: Well, I know something that isn’t down to luck, Neil – the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尼尔，我知道有一件事不是凭运气的——你那个问题的答案。

sentences.en: Ah yes. I asked you about the origin of the term play date.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。我问过你“play date”这个词的起源。

sentences.en: Which country does it come from? I think it's the USA.
sentences.zh: 它来自哪个国家？我觉得是美国。

sentences.en: Well Beth, you are right. [Yay!] So well done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，贝丝，你答对了。[耶！]干得漂亮。

sentences.en: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, ‘play date’ was first used in the Lincoln Daily Star newspaper in Nebraska, USA in 1915.
sentences.zh: 根据《牛津英语词典》，“play date”一词于 1915 年首次使用于美国内布拉斯加州的《林肯每日星报》（Lincoln Daily Star）。

sentences.en: OK, let’s recap the vocabulary we’ve learned, starting with play date – an arrangement that parents make for their young children to play together.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们复习一下学过的词汇，首先是“play date”——父母为年幼的孩子们安排的一起玩耍的活动。

sentences.en: A clique is a small group of people who spend a lot of time together and may seem unfriendly towards other people.
sentences.zh: “Clique”（小圈子）是一小群经常待在一起、对其他人可能显得不太友好的人。

sentences.en: Glam is short for glamorous, meaning visually attractive and exciting.
sentences.zh: “Glam”是 glamorous 的缩写，意思是视觉上吸引人且令人兴奋。

sentences.en: If you fit into a group of people, you belong and feel accepted by them because you’re similar to them.
sentences.zh: 如果你“fit into”（融入）一个群体，说明你属于该群体并因与他们相似而感到被接纳。

sentences.en: If you say something is down to luck, you mean that it depends on chance or luck, rather than any skill or effort you make.
sentences.zh: 如果你说某事是“down to luck”（凭运气），意思是它取决于机缘或运气，而不是你的任何技巧或努力。

sentences.en: And finally, if you click with someone, you feel a friendly and positive connection when you meet them for the first time.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你和某人“click”（一拍即合），说明你初次见到他们时就感受到了友好和积极的联结。

sentences.en: Once again our time is up. Why not head over to the 6 Minute English website to find a quiz and worksheet for this programme while it’s still fresh in your mind.
sentences.zh: 我们的时间又到了。趁着记忆犹新，去“6分钟英语”网站找找这期节目的测试题和练习册吧。

sentences.en: See you again soon, goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 我们很快再见，今天就到这里！拜拜！
